items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: you could say, “Hey Jim, turn it down a little bit.”

ctx.x: I see. But generally speaking the jazz records, the jazz recordings took less time and I’m wondering, with Cannonball, would they play a tune and finish it and then come into the booth and like check it out, then say okay?

No. Everybody’s always checking it out. I mean right? In the studio they might work if you’ve got a group, and they might work on a tune for 15, 20 minutes. And you get your thing together in 20 minutes. I mean the guys out there, they’re not really interested in what you’re doing other than the fact that they want their phones to sound right. So really immediately when you’re starting a date immediately you’ve got to make the phones © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

right. They haven’t played two bars yet and they’re complaining about the phones. I would say, take the phones off, you know, let me get a balance and then we’ll go for it — and then you can ask more bass, more this more that. At least you get an engineer — I’ve never had trouble with the players. I know engineers have trouble with players. My feeling about rhythm sections was always not to put them all in booths all over the room but to put them together in a room so they’re all facing each other. So if it’s a…
